fields.description:
## Context

The DSO orchestrator agent loses context window to sub-agent draft outputs during sprint runs. `/dso:preplanning` sub-agent calls (story decomposition, adversarial red-team review) and `/dso:implementation-plan` sub-agent calls (architectural review, plan-review, gap analysis) return large draft bodies that flow through the orchestrator transcript before being acted on. The existing remediation pattern — passing artifact file paths via `--artifact <path>` — is partial: 5 known sites today (3 in implementation-plan, 1 in preplanning, 1 in sprint's story-verifier cycle). The orchestrator pays the context cost every cycle, which pushes it toward compaction earlier than necessary and degrades recall of session-spanning state.

Affected users: (a) the DSO orchestrator agent itself, which runs out of usable context window faster than necessary; (b) indirectly the human running `/dso:sprint`, who pays token cost and feels degraded behavior when the orchestrator approaches compaction. SC7 below is the load-bearing user-impact signal.

EPIC_CLASS: class:architectural

## Approach

CLI-thin, prompt-heavy: add a deterministic `dso ticket scratch` subcommand family (`set` / `get` / `clear`) and a `--include-scratch` flag on `dso ticket show`. Storage at `.tickets-tracker/.scratch/<ticket-id>/<key>` (gitignored on the tickets branch; symlink-shared across sibling worktrees via the existing `.tickets-tracker/` symlink mechanism). Each scratch entry is a JSON envelope `{ts, value}`. `get` returns structured JSON with `status: "hit"` or `"miss"` (exit 0 in both cases) so sub-agents can deterministically fail back to the orchestrator on miss. Migration rewires the 5 named `--artifact <path>` sub-agent-prompt handoff sites (`implementation-plan/SKILL.md:511`, `:978`, `:1238`; `preplanning/SKILL.md:513`; `sprint/SKILL.md:2332`) to write payloads via `scratch set` and return short receipts (`ticket_id`, `key`, `byte_count`). Cleanup is load-bearing on `ticket transition … closed` and on `ticket archive`; `scratch clear` is exposed for convenience but is not load-bearing.

## Success Criteria

1. CLI surface behaves as specified: `dso ticket scratch set <id> <key> <value>` writes a JSON envelope; `get <id> <key>` returns `{"status":"hit","ts":<iso8601>,"value":<value>}` on hit or `{"status":"miss","ticket_id":<id>,"key":<key>}` on miss, exit 0 in both cases; `clear <id> [<key>]` removes one or all; `dso ticket show <id> --include-scratch` adds a `scratch` object to the existing JSON output.

2. Migration is complete: All 5 named `--artifact <path>` sub-agent-prompt handoff sites (implementation-plan/SKILL.md:511, :978, :1238; preplanning/SKILL.md:513; sprint/SKILL.md:2332) are converted to `scratch set/get`. `grep -- '--artifact ' plugins/dso/skills/{preplanning,implementation-plan,sprint}/SKILL.md` returns zero matches for sub-agent-prompt handoffs (matches for `--artifact-file=` or `--artifacts-dir` helper-script args are out of scope).

3. Sub-agent return contract enforces receipt-only AND orchestrator-side validation: (a) for each migrated call site, the sub-agent return contract documented in the SKILL.md specifies the receipt object (fields: `ticket_id`, `key`, `byte_count`) and explicitly excludes the draft body; (b) the orchestrator-side dispatch logic in the same SKILL.md validates each sub-agent return against the receipt schema and emits `RECEIPT_PARSE_ERROR` (logged and escalated) when the return contains anything other than the receipt object, rather than silently passing the key forward to the next sub-agent.

4. Cleanup on close: after `dso ticket transition <id> <prev-status> closed`, `.tickets-tracker/.scratch/<id>/` no longer exists.

5. Cleanup on archive: after `dso ticket archive <id>`, `.tickets-tracker/.scratch/<id>/` no longer exists.

6. Sync isolation: the Jira reconciler payload builder reads zero bytes from `.tickets-tracker/.scratch/`. The path is excluded from the tickets-branch git history (added to the tickets-worktree's `.git/info/exclude`).

7. Context cost reduction confirmed in-session: a measurement harness captures the orchestrator-transcript token count for sub-agent return blocks at each of the 5 migrated sites against a fixed test epic, on pre-migration HEAD and on post-migration HEAD. Post-migration cumulative return-block token count is at least 70% lower than pre-migration for the same epic. (Conservative threshold — actual reduction expected near 98% since the receipt is 3 fields vs. multi-KB drafts; 70% leaves headroom for measurement noise.)

## State Lifecycle

| Variable | CREATE | UPDATE | CONSUME | RETIRE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.tickets-tracker/.scratch/<ticket-id>/<key>` (one file per key, JSON envelope) | `dso ticket scratch set` (called by sub-agents in preplanning, implementation-plan, sprint) | `dso ticket scratch set` (overwrite of existing key) | `dso ticket scratch get` (orchestrator / next sub-agent in handoff); `dso ticket show --include-scratch` (humans, debugging) | `dso ticket transition <id> ... closed` (load-bearing); `dso ticket archive <id>` (load-bearing, defense in depth); `dso ticket scratch clear <id> [<key>]` (non-load-bearing convenience) |

## Scenario Analysis

- Concurrent sub-agent writes to same (ticket_id, key) under parallel dispatch (runtime, high) — out of scope per design; namespaced keys mitigate.
- Partial write leaves corrupt JSON envelope on crash mid-write (runtime, medium) — atomic write-to-temp-then-rename required at implementation time.
- Existing tickets-tracker worktrees lack .scratch/ exclusion after upgrade (deployment, high) — `ticket-init.sh` must be idempotent and add the exclusion entry on re-run.
- Key namespace collisions across the 5 migrated call sites (configuration, high) — key-namespace convention required (e.g., `<skill>:<step>:<purpose>`).
- Unbounded scratch value size exhausts tickets-tracker disk (configuration, medium) — implementation should impose a max-byte limit with clear error envelope.
- `scratch get` exit 0 on miss bypasses shell error handling in callers (configuration, high) — sub-agent prompts MUST parse JSON status field, not exit code.
- Ticket IDs containing path-traversal characters bypass directory scoping (configuration, medium) — input validation on ticket_id/key charset required.
- Assumption: tickets-tracker-guard hook does not block CLI in-process I/O (assumption, high) — verified during this brainstorm; document the contract.
- Assumption: dispatch model serializes writes to same (ticket_id, key) (assumption, high) — declared out of scope by design; namespaced keys prevent collision in practice.
- Assumption: cleanup-on-close path runs even on abnormal ticket transitions (assumption, medium) — `dso ticket archive` marks `status=deleted` + `archived=True`, so SC5 covers the delete-equivalent path.
- Assumption: .tickets-tracker/ symlink mechanism is consistent across all worktree creation paths (assumption, high) — general worktree-lifecycle invariant; not scratch-specific.
- Assumption: Jira reconciler payload builder will continue to ignore .scratch/ (assumption, critical) — SC6 explicitly verifies zero-bytes-read; a directory-walk regression would fail SC6.
- Assumption: sub-agents will correctly parse the {status:hit|miss} JSON envelope (assumption, high) — addressed by Prompt Alignment Findings 1, 2 below.

## Research Findings

- Jira issue-properties analog: 32KB cap per key, last-write-wins concurrency, no built-in merge. Argues for namespaced keys per call-site (not shared keys) and a writer-identity field for debuggability. Source: Jira Cloud platform — Entity properties.
- GitHub Actions outputs-vs-artifacts precedent: small structured receipts in the new channel; size cutover threshold above which call-sites continue using a filesystem path; during migration run both channels in parallel with deprecation log on the old channel to avoid breaking in-flight sessions. Sources: GitHub Actions documentation on storing and sharing data.

## Prior-Art Findings

- LangGraph supervisor scratchpad + Command pattern: workers append structured updates to shared state and return Command objects combining state mutation with control flow. Validates the scratch CLI as shared-state equivalent and the typed-receipt-return shape.
- Memory Pointer pattern (arXiv 2511.22729): tools store large outputs in external state and return short reference keys; ~7× token reduction. Direct precedent for the receipt-only contract.
- Typed-interface + explicit miss signaling discipline: sub-agents must declare typed outputs and signal failure explicitly (no silent empty returns); orchestrator owns retry/fallback. Validates the `{status:hit|miss}` envelope and `SCRATCH_MISS` return-to-orchestrator pattern.

## Prompt Alignment Findings

Carry these into preplanning and implementation-plan as the contract for how the 5 migrated SKILL.md sites must be rewritten:

1. Co-locate the SCRATCH_MISS guard with the `scratch get` invocation (not in a preamble or protocol section). The conditional branch must be structurally adjacent to the tool call it governs. (Instruction Locality.)

2. Add an explicit negative example showing that `{"status":"miss"}` is NOT a valid input payload. One-line addition in the `scratch get` instruction block. (Structured-output disambiguation on the input side.)

3. Replace the receipt-only negative instruction with: (a) an `<output_contract>` XML tag at prompt start declaring "Your entire response MUST be a single JSON object matching this schema: {ticket_id, key, byte_count}. Any other text — including the draft body you produced — must be written to the scratch store, not returned in your response."; (b) an end-of-block reinforcement immediately before the return instruction restating the suppression. (Verbosity + Instruction Locality.)

4. Namespace-prefix the routing identifiers as `SCRATCH_TICKET_ID` / `SCRATCH_KEY` in the orchestrator-to-sub-agent prompt to eliminate collision with other ticket IDs mentioned in the same prompt (work ticket, parent epic, story ID). (Instruction Leaking.)

5. Enumerate cleanup actions inline in the SCRATCH_MISS exit branch (e.g., "no scratch write needed — nothing was produced"); do not rely on a trailing cleanup section being reached from an early-exit path. (Multi-Step Reasoning Drift / Instruction Locality on early-exit cleanup.)

## Dependencies

None. SC6 applies to whichever Jira reconciler implementation is current at merge time; the relationship with open epic 4047-3cb1-6cb4-46a1 (Derivable level-triggered Jira reconciler) is parallel-safe, not a hard dependency.
